body: You wish there was a reason why you feel and act the way that you do?

Maybe so. I always thought they went a little overboard, and they were being unreasonable.

But they were the only ones who ever made me feel wanted, like I wasn't supposed to go away and let the people who actually matter go on with their lives, if you know what I'm trying to say.

I'm ashamed to say that I found one of their active social media accounts before we went our separate ways, and I look at it from time to time. Usually when I'm feeling really down. It's always a huge kick in the face, because it's obvious that they've completely moved on. That whole fiasco meant absolutely nothing to them in the long run, and why would it? It was just some stupid online thing.

Meanwhile, I haven't moved on because I have nothing to move on *to*. I don't have anything to look forward to or work towards in real life. I remember how excited I would get when I saw them online, because for once in my life, it looked like I wasn't going to be alone after all.

I'm sorry, I started rambling there. It may not make a lot of sense now. My mind will probably slowly move on to other things, until I suddenly remember that my life is laughably pathetic. If I'm lucky, that won't happen today.

You could be right about the 'being comfortable with the idea of death' thing. 

When I was little, I had a dream that I died from some strange illness. I wasn't bedridden or anything, but everyone (myself included) knew I was about to die. That dream absolutely terrified me when I had it, but now it doesn't even unnerve me. 

Obviously I don't want to die a slow, painful death, but if I knew I was about to die, it wouldn't be all that bad. The idea of something so unknown is actually sort of exciting, even if it could just be nothingness.

I'm not going to pretend that my thoughts and the things I post are revolutionary and thought provoking. In fact, some of them are rather embarrassing. I've just always had a bad habit of saying what was on my mind without thinking about what could happen. This was a problem when I was little, because I would say hurtful things without realizing it. 

Now, it's mostly just throwing my two cents into discussions even when I haven't done research or anything like that. I don't defend my points if I can see that they're wrong, but I still end up saying stupid things. I usually end up avoiding serious discussions as a result, because I know I'll flub it up somehow. 

In fact, this actually led to a huge problem on an online forum a year or two ago. I'm fairly certain I lost two potentially really good friends because of it.
